description: Graduate methods course on studying software and its makers with evidence: experiments, surveys, case studies, literature reviews, repository mining and the statistics that go with them. Students design studies, mine real git histories, run the analyses in code, and judge validity and replicability of published work.
modelledOn: Wohlin et al., Experimentation in Software Engineering
Shull, Singer and Sjoberg (eds.), Guide to Advanced Empirical Software Engineering
Kitchenham and Charters, Guidelines for Performing Systematic Literature Reviews in Software Engineering
Runeson et al., Case Study Research in Software Engineering
outcomes: Formulate software engineering research questions as testable hypotheses and choose a fitting research strategy.
Design and analyse a controlled experiment, including treatment allocation, power and effect size.
Plan a systematic literature review or mapping study with a documented protocol and quality assessment.
Mine a version control repository to build a dataset and state the biases in it.
Select and apply appropriate statistical tests, effect sizes and intervals, and interpret them without over-claiming.
Critique the validity and replicability of a published empirical study and report your own results transparently.

units.title: Science and measurement in software engineering
topics: The scientific method in software engineering: theories, research questions and hypotheses
Research paradigms: positivist, interpretivist and design science
Research strategies compared: experiment, survey, case study, action research and field study
Measurement theory: scale types, reliability, validity and the goal-question-metric approach
Research ethics: informed consent, anonymising developer data and the ethics of mining public repositories

units.title: Software metrics and their limits
topics: Size and complexity metrics: lines of code, cyclomatic complexity and Halstead measures
Object-oriented metrics: coupling, cohesion and the Chidamber-Kemerer suite
Process metrics: code churn, ownership, developer turnover and the bus factor
Defect metrics and defect prediction models: precision, recall and cross-project transfer
Metric pitfalls: construct validity, Goodhart law and gaming of measures

units.title: Controlled experiments
topics: Hypotheses, independent and dependent variables, treatments and confounders
Experimental designs: between-subjects, within-subjects, factorial, crossover and Latin square
Participants: students versus professionals, sampling and recruitment, including in Ghana
Threats in human-subject experiments: learning effects, fatigue, experimenter bias
Running and analysing an experiment: pilot, instrumentation, pre-registration and reporting
Quasi-experiments, A/B tests and natural experiments in industry

units.title: Surveys, case studies and qualitative methods
topics: Survey design: sampling frames, response rates and non-response bias
Questionnaire construction and the analysis of Likert-scale data
Case study research: protocol, units of analysis, propositions and evidence chains
Interviews, thematic analysis and coding in the style of grounded theory
Triangulation and mixed-methods designs

units.title: Systematic literature reviews and mapping studies
topics: Review protocol: research questions, search strings and databases
Study selection, quality assessment and data extraction forms; inter-rater agreement
Snowballing and systematic mapping studies versus full reviews
Synthesis: narrative, thematic and quantitative meta-analysis of effect sizes
Grey literature, tertiary studies and the limits of publication-biased evidence

units.title: Mining software repositories
topics: Data sources: git history, issue trackers, code review systems and package registries
Extracting history with git; the SZZ algorithm for bug-introducing commits
Cleaning mined data: identity merging, bots, time zones and tangled changes
Sampling bias in repository studies: forks, toy projects, time-travel and survivorship
Text mining of commit messages and issue reports
Software ecosystems: dependency graphs, release cadence and developer community analysis

units.title: Statistical analysis
topics: Descriptive statistics, distributions and checking assumptions
Hypothesis tests: t-test, Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon and chi-square; statistical power and sample size
Effect sizes and intervals: Cohen d, Cliff delta, Vargha-Delaney A and confidence intervals
Regression: linear, logistic and mixed-effects models for repeated measures
Multiple comparisons, p-hacking, and an introduction to Bayesian estimation
Resampling: bootstrap and permutation tests

units.title: Validity, replication and reporting
topics: Threats to validity: internal, external, construct and conclusion
Replication, reproducibility and open science: registered reports and artefact evaluation
Reporting guidelines and writing for a peer-reviewed venue
From evidence to practice: evidence briefings for engineering managers
Mini research project: design, execute and report a small empirical study

schedule.title: Research questions, strategies and ethics
schedule.exercise: Turn a practitioner worry (does code review slow delivery?) into a research question, hypothesis, strategy and goal-question-metric tree, and list the ethical issues of using public developer data.

tasks.title: Build a goal-question-metric tree for the claim that pair programming improves quality, choosing measures and scale types in the scenario rubric
Choose the research strategy for five research questions and justify what each strategy can and cannot show, scored against expert answers
Decide how to handle an ethics case about scraping developer emails and mining a private Ghanaian company repository, and defend your consent plan

schedule.title: Metrics and defect prediction
schedule.exercise: Compute metrics on a small program, then explain how each one could be gamed and what construct it fails to capture.

tasks.title: Write a script that computes lines of code and cyclomatic complexity for ten functions and flags those above a threshold of 10
Train a logistic defect predictor on module metrics, report precision and recall and compare with the always-defective baseline
Show Goodhart effect: optimise a team to a coverage target in a simulated project and measure how defect detection changes versus true quality

schedule.title: Experimental design and participants
schedule.exercise: Design a within-subjects experiment comparing two code review checklists, with counterbalancing, a power analysis and a recruitment plan for 24 student participants.

tasks.title: Generate a Latin square allocation of three tools to three task sets for 12 participants and check each order appears equally often
List the variables, treatments and confounders of a test-driven development experiment and fix the design so a flagged confound is controlled
Run a power analysis for a two-group experiment at effect sizes 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8 and chart sample size per group against power

schedule.title: Analysis, pre-registration and quasi-experiments
schedule.exercise: Write the pre-registration for the review checklist experiment, listing analysis plan and stopping rule, and compare it with an A/B test on an app.

tasks.title: Identify the threats in a flawed experiment report (learning effect, unequal experience, experimenter bias) and propose one fix per threat
Simulate a pilot, compute the variance, and revise the sample size plan, writing out the analysis script before seeing the main data
Analyse a simulated A/B test of a mobile money app screen with sequential looks, and show how peeking inflates the false positive rate

schedule.title: Surveys, case studies and qualitative analysis
schedule.exercise: Design a survey of Ghanaian developers on testing practices, then code ten interview excerpts into themes and write a short case study protocol.

tasks.title: Summarise Likert responses from 60 developers with medians and stacked percentage bars, and say why the mean is questionable
Simulate a survey with 30 percent response and a biased non-response mechanism, and measure how far the estimate is from the true value
Code interview excerpts into themes with a codebook, resolve disagreement with a second coder and report agreement using Cohen kappa

schedule.title: Review protocol and study selection
schedule.exercise: Write a review protocol on microservice migration with research questions, search string, inclusion criteria, quality checklist and extraction form.

tasks.title: Run Boolean searches over a table of 500 paper records, record hits for three search strings and choose the best on precision against a known set
Apply inclusion and exclusion criteria to 100 records in SQL, log reasons for each exclusion and report the screening flow counts
Run backward and forward snowballing over a citation graph from five seed papers and measure how many known relevant papers it finds beyond the search

schedule.title: Evidence synthesis and publication bias
schedule.exercise: Pool the effect sizes from eight studies of pair programming, draw a funnel plot to look for publication bias, and write the limitations of the synthesis.

tasks.title: Plot a forest plot of eight standardised mean differences and read the pooled estimate with its confidence interval
Compute a random-effects pooled effect and the I-squared statistic for the eight studies, and run a leave-one-out sensitivity check
Draw a funnel plot, test its asymmetry, and simulate how unpublished null results would change the pooled estimate

schedule.title: Mining git history
schedule.exercise: Extract a year of history from a repository, rebuild bug-fixing and bug-introducing commits with SZZ, and document the cleaning steps and data you removed.

tasks.title: Use git log with format options to list commits per author per month for a sample repository and save the counts
Trace a bug fix with git blame to find the commit that introduced the faulty line, then record both commits in the dataset
Merge developer identities with name and email heuristics, remove bot accounts, and report how the top-10 contributor ranking changes

schedule.title: Biases, text mining and ecosystems
schedule.exercise: Draw a sample of repositories two ways and compare them, classify commit messages with keywords, and sketch a dependency network of a package ecosystem.

tasks.title: Classify 200 commit messages into bug fix, feature and refactoring by keyword rules and report accuracy against hand labels
Compare a random sample and a most-starred sample of repositories on size, age and activity, and list the biases each introduces
Build a dependency graph from package manifests, find the most depended-on packages, and simulate the impact of removing one critical package

schedule.title: Choosing tests and effect sizes
schedule.exercise: For three datasets pick the right test, check assumptions, report the effect size with an interval and write the interpretation in plain words.

tasks.title: Describe a skewed dataset of review times with histogram, median and interquartile range, and test for normality
Compare two groups of task completion times with a t-test and a Mann-Whitney test, and explain why the results differ on skewed data
Compute Cohen d, Cliff delta and a bootstrap confidence interval for two groups, and write the report sentence a reviewer would accept

schedule.title: Regression, multiple comparisons and resampling
schedule.exercise: Fit a logistic regression for defect-proneness, correct for multiple comparisons in a table of 20 tests, and use a permutation test to check a claim.

tasks.title: Fit a linear regression of bug count on size and churn for 100 modules and interpret each coefficient with its interval
Run 20 tests on random data, count false positives at 0.05, and apply Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections to compare
Use a permutation test and bootstrap to analyse repeated measures from a crossover experiment, and compare with a mixed-effects model

schedule.title: Validity, replication and reporting
schedule.exercise: Critique a published study on its four validity threats, attempt to reproduce one table from its shared data, and draft a reporting checklist.

tasks.title: Classify ten stated limitations of a study into internal, external, construct and conclusion validity threats
Reproduce a results table from a shared dataset and analysis script, record each discrepancy and decide whether it matters
Peer review a flawed paper in the scenario engine, listing validity threats, unsupported claims and the reanalysis that would settle them

schedule.title: Evidence into practice and the mini project
schedule.exercise: Present the mini project: question, design, data, analysis, threats and an evidence briefing for a software manager.

tasks.title: Write a half-page evidence briefing for a manager on whether code review reduces defects, and have it scored for accuracy and over-claiming
Run the planned analysis for your mini project end to end from raw data to figures, and check it reruns from a clean start
Test the robustness of your mini project result by varying filtering rules, models and outlier handling, and report which conclusions survive
